title: Latin cipher postscript on Şerban Cantacuzino and Antide Dunod, Wallachia, after Oct. 1688, Biblioteka Kórnicka BK 1560 (WBC edition 343124, 'List zaszyfrowany')

documents.route: unknown writer in the service of a 'Celsissimus Princeps' (probably Constantin Brâncoveanu) to a 'Reverendissimus Pater'

plaintext.source: contemporary interlinear decipherment of every cipher run except code group 202

transcription.source: every cipher run and its gloss transcribed from the WBC DjVu scans decoded to PNG (runs.tsv)
transcription.notes: Measured 439 digit tokens = 436 two-digit cipher signs + 2 three-digit code groups (202, 203) + 1 heavily struck single digit in 'audi2?et'. Clear word endings inside cipher runs are not counted.

system.summary: Mixed-order substitution of single letters by two-digit numbers 12-51 (one number per letter, a separate number for the ae-diphthong e), used for words inside clear Latin, with three-digit code groups.
system.notes: Endings and single letters of cipher words are often left in clear; y is written in clear. Only two code groups occur (203 = liter-, 202 unglossed).

prior_solution.where: contemporary interlinear decipherment on the manuscript itself (every run but code group 202); no printed edition found

conditions.human_role: Project-level: set up Claude Code with Opus 5.5 and posed the catalogue entry with /goal. No target-specific intervention recorded.

solution.what: Found the WBC edition 343124 ('List zaszyfrowany') in the BK 1560 structure; passed the site's proof-of-work check in the browser pane and downloaded the three DjVu pages with its cookie.
No DjVu tool installed; bundled the DjVu.js library (npm djvujs-dist) with esbuild and decoded the pages in Node to PNG.
Viewed the pages: clear Latin postscript with struck-through two-digit number runs, each glossed interlinearly in a second hand.
Transcribed all 70 cipher runs with their glosses from 1700-px bands and native-resolution zooms (runs.tsv).
decode.py aligned runs with glosses and built the key: 22 numbers, one letter each, no conflicts; 15 only for the ae-diphthong.

Deciphered every run with the key alone and compared with the gloss: 61/70 identical; the 9 others are a code group, writer slips (functsm, pricipem, defunct, one struck digit) and glosser normalisations (gerent, sollicitaverant, Gergenbeio).

Identified 'Burgundus Antidius Dunod' as Antide Dunod SJ, imperial envoy to Wallachia 1687-88, and 'defunctum Principem Serbanum' as Şerban Cantacuzino (d. 29 Oct 1688); searched for a printed edition of the letter and for Gegenbey/Gityk, none found.
Wrote out the whole postscript, clear and deciphered, with a translation (reading.md); code group 202 left open.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): linked runs.tsv (every run with its contemporary gloss) and ct.txt as transcription, reading.md (with translation) as decryption; key_file key.tsv

Brice Dudout (Claude Opus 5.5): independent decoder (verify_dudout_20261114.py) reading only key.tsv, run on the 70 cipher runs of runs.tsv: 436 two-digit signs (one doubtful, 12?), 1 struck single digit and 2 code groups, 439 tokens as in ct.txt. With u/v and ae/e taken as equal, 60 runs give the gloss letter for letter; the other 10 are code groups 203 and 202 and the eight writer or glosser slips already listed in NOTES.md (gerant, solicitaverant, Gegenbeio, Gegenbeii, functsm, pricipem, defunct, audi2?et). No key value is contradicted. README read bar recount (research/reading_audit/v10_relabel.measure on reading.md): 0.986 over 778 words, as recorded. The WBC scans sit behind a proof-of-work page and were not re-read.

outcome.method_basis: Every cipher run but one carries a contemporary interlinear decipherment; the key rebuilt from it here reproduces each gloss from the numbers alone.
outcome.fraction_read_source: targets/szembek1689/ct.txt, 439 digit tokens; unread: code group 202 and the struck digit in audi2?et (its letter r comes from the gloss)

gaps.detail: occurs once, no gloss, no code table

outcome.notes: Read at the time; key rebuilt and checked here. Catalogue 348's 'unknown to the Szembek family, early 18th c.' corrected: Wallachian court after Şerban Cantacuzino's death (Oct 1688), denouncing Antide Dunod SJ. Postscript only; the letter's main body is not in the item.

texts.label: BK 1560 'List zaszyfrowany', Latin cipher postscript, after Oct 1688
texts.summary: A writer in the service of a 'Celsissimus Princeps' (most likely Constantin Brâncoveanu) thanks a 'Reverendissimus Pater', protests the Wallachian side's sincerity against imperial broken promises, and denounces Antide Dunod as an impostor who misled the late Prince Şerban Cantacuzino; he adds that Gegenbey was killed by a false friend's treachery.
